claims.text: Conventional additive manufacturing of AlCrFeNiSi powder feedstock produces coarse microstructures.
Conventional additive manufacturing of AlCrFeNiSi produces high residual thermal stresses.
Conventional additive manufacturing of AlCrFeNiSi produces suboptimal mechanical properties.
The proposed intervention is selective laser melting with the build plate maintained at approximately -150 °C.
Cryogenic build-plate cooling will refine the AlCrFeNiSi microstructure.
The refined microstructure will contain finer grains.
Rapid solidification under cryogenic build-plate cooling will produce finer grains.
Cryogenic build-plate cooling will reduce thermal gradients during solidification.
Cryogenic build-plate cooling will minimize thermal-expansion mismatch during solidification.
Reduced thermal gradients will lower residual stresses.
Minimizing thermal-expansion mismatch during solidification will lower residual stresses.
Cryogenic cooling will curb the formation of coarse microstructural features.
Coarse microstructural features compromise mechanical performance.
Cryogenically cooled components will have lower residual stresses than room-temperature-build-plate controls.
Cryogenically cooled components will have higher yield strength than room-temperature-build-plate controls.
Cryogenically cooled components will have higher hardness than room-temperature-build-plate controls.
Cryogenically cooled components will have more uniform microstructures than room-temperature-build-plate controls.
The effect is expected to be significant for AlCrFeNiSi miniature components with features on the order of a few millimeters.
The predicted effect may not translate directly to larger components or other alloy systems.
